newsitem.title: USA: Union Acceptance eyes loan acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Union Acceptance eyes loan acquisitions.

text.p: Union Acceptance Corp said Wednesday it is continuing to focus on increasing loan acquisition volume with strong underlying credit quality.
The company said loan acquisitions for the first quarter ended September 30 totalled more than $296.6 million, up 24 percent from $239.8 acquired for the quarter last year.

"Increased loan acquisition volume is attributable to both market expansion and market penetration," said John Stainbrook, Union's president, adding that over the past year, the company added more than 750 new dealers and entered several new markets.
"We will continue to support controlled growth of the company in conjunction with a strong focus on the underlying credit quality of the portfolio," he said.

At September 30, 1996, delinquencies related to prime auto receivables improved to 2.02 percent of the the total servicing portfolio, from 3.06 percent last year. Delinquencies on non-prime auto receivables improved to 3.20 percent at September 30, 1996, from 4.86 percent in 1995.
